clue.text: Busy in England, grew old

parts.note: to have grown old is to have aged

explanation.surface: Someone is kept busy in England while getting on in years.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone line that is in use is busy, the British term for which is engaged.

clue.text: Clown doesn't finish off opponent

indicators.note: the clown's word is not allowed to reach its end, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: an antic is an old word for a buffoon or clown

explanation.surface: A clown fails to complete the job of polishing off a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is a link word here, though it tempts as part of 'finish off'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is against a cause or person is an opponent of it, as a preposition or noun.

clue.text: Examination of really odd pieces

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the run of words are the odd-numbered pieces taken

explanation.surface: Someone sits an exam made up of strange bits and pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: From 'of really', take letters 1, 3, 5 and 7: O, R, A, L.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, such as a viva or language exam, is an examination by mouth.

clue.text: I felt he'd upset everybody competing

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker felt that some man had upset all the other competitors.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing, all the runners in a race other than the favourite, or all entrants together, are collectively the field.

clue.text: Girl on a roll, she makes record

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
a roll, as in a roll of names, is a list

explanation.surface: A girl on a winning streak is setting a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a down-clue link: ANN sits on top of A LIST. 'Roll' tempts as a winning streak; it is a register of names.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicler writes yearly records of events, and a woman doing so makes a record.

clue.text: Knight enthralled by foreign niece's clothing accessory from America

indicators.note: to be enthralled is to be held captive, so the knight's letters are held inside the other piece
foreign suggests the letters become strange or alien, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
KT is the abbreviation for a knight, as in Knight of the Thistle

explanation.surface: A knight is captivated by a foreign niece's American fashion accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' makes NECIE from NIECE, and 'enthralled by' puts KT inside it. The possessive 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie worn round the neck is a fashion item, the full name being a chiefly American usage.

clue.text: Data needed for admin form

indicators.note: the letters are needed to make up the clue words, so they are found within them

explanation.surface: Information has to be supplied to complete an administrative form.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is a short form of information, which is to say facts or data.

clue.text: Love unchanging fertile spot

parts.note: love is a zero score in tennis, written as the letter O
something left as it is stays unchanged

explanation.surface: Love remains constant in a fruitful place.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile area in a desert where water is found is an oasis.

clue.text: Playing in Bath, reran bygone work

annotationWithheld.why: Playing in Bath, reran bygone work: the anagram of BATH RERAN BYGONE gives the full title across 9-across and 14-down, but the puzzle file does not link them, so the leftover five letters cannot be quoted
annotationWithheld.clue: Playing in Bath, reran bygone work

clue.text: A film ends in riot in Midlands town

indicators.note: letters in a riot are in uproar and disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film ends amid rioting in an English Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: Mansfield is a town in Nottinghamshire, England; with 11 across it makes another Austen title.
explanation.definitionFit: Mansfield is a market town in Nottinghamshire, in the East Midlands of England.

clue.text: He explored area of open land

definitions.meaning: Mungo ... was a Scottish explorer of the Niger in Africa
a public green space in a town

explanation.surface: An explorer surveys some open countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mungo Park was a Scottish explorer of West Africa, and a park is a green public space.

clue.text: See 4
Hearing maybe last bits of tedious discourse on dress code

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone listens to the tail end of a dull lecture about dress codes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing is one of the five faculties of perception, so it is an example.

clue.text: Receptacle for litter, I note, is in centre of gaol from the start

indicators.note: these pieces sit in the middle of the other part
the central pair of letters of the word gaol is taken

parts.note: a bin holds rubbish
ti (or te) is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A rubbish bin is found in the middle of a prison from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of gaol' gives AO; BIN, I and TI go between those letters. Gaol is the British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means from the beginning.

clue.text: See 9

annotationWithheld.why: See 9: second part of the 9-across title, whose clue's anagram covers both lights though the puzzle file does not group them

clue.text: Naughty sex names used by uncultured guy from near London?

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters are made to misbehave and change order

explanation.surface: Smutty insults are used by a boorish chap from the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex Man is a British stereotype of a brash, materialistic working-class man from the county of Essex, just east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The stereotype names a brash and philistine type from the county bordering London, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Singular by-line, is it designed to show awareness?

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: designed means planned or arranged, so these letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A journalist wonders whether a single byline was planned to show perceptiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' turns BY-LINE IS IT into ENSIBILITY, after S. 'to show' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensitivity, a keen responsiveness to feeling, is a kind of awareness.

clue.text: First light in such a place?

definitions.text: First light in such a place?

parts.words: First light in such a place?
parts.note: dawn arrives earliest at the furthest point toward the sunrise, so the place that sees first light is the furthest east

explanation.surface: Where is the place that sees the sun rise first?
explanation.definitionFit: The location furthest toward the rising sun is the most easterly one.

clue.text: Dubious, led a gel astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A dubious leader took someone off the right path.
explanation.walkthrough: The page as read has 'get'; the anagram needs 'gel', since the answer has two Ls and no T.
explanation.definitionFit: Claimed but unproven, as with a supposed crime, is doubtful.

clue.text: School about to dip into uplifting musical work

indicators.note: the short piece dips into the middle of the other word
in a down clue, lifting up means reading from the bottom upward, so backwards

parts.note: an etude is a study composed for practice
CA is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A teacher plans to dip into an uplifting piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns ETUDE into EDUTE; 'to dip into' puts CA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or train them.

clue.text: One with great desire gets in by bullying

indicators.note: one piece gets into the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: a luster is someone who lusts

explanation.surface: A covetous person gets ahead by intimidation.
explanation.definitionFit: Blustering speech is loud and threatening, much like browbeating.

clue.text: Quiet journey for group of animals

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft
a ride is a trip

explanation.surface: A peaceful trip to see a herd of wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: A family of lions is collectively termed a pride.

clue.text: Bill drawn into port set

indicators.note: the bill is pulled inside the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
an ad, or advertisement, is a bill posted up

explanation.surface: A bill is pulled into a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireless receiver is a radio set.

clue.text: She sends writer back to mother?

indicators.note: the writer's word is sent back, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a setter refers to themself as me
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A girl sends a letter-writer home to her mum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sends ... back' turns ME into EM. 'She' stands for a woman's name, also the title of an Austen novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a female given name, so a woman who could be called by the pronoun.

clue.text: Intolerance the cost when biased judge (no good) is brought in

indicators.note: the altered judge is brought inside the cost

parts.note: the price is what something costs

indicators.note: biased means slanted out of true, so the remaining letters are skewed into a new order
no good means the G (good) is removed

explanation.surface: Intolerance costs dear when a partial judge is drafted in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' takes G from JUDGE, leaving JUDE; 'biased' makes EJUD, which 'is brought in' places inside PRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigotry, an unjust preconceived opinion, is intolerance.

clue.text: For the most part regretful loss of position

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, so the last letter goes

parts.note: ruing means regretting

explanation.surface: Mostly regretful at having lost status.
explanation.definitionFit: Downfall, such as a fall from rank or fortune, is a loss of standing.

clue.text: Lady extremely nice after indication of agreement in Hamburg

indicators.note: after places the trimmed word nice second, behind the German yes

parts.note: ja is German for yes

indicators.note: the extreme ends of the word nice are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A very pleasant woman follows a German yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so a woman.

clue.text: See 15
"Raise Son up" could lead to religious faith?

indicators.note: the words could lead to a new word once their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bringing a son up might steer him toward a religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A persuasion is a set of beliefs, especially a religious denomination.

clue.text: Chooses organisations promoting top standards first of all

indicators.note: the first letter of each word is taken, so all their firsts

explanation.surface: Groups that promote high standards make their selections.
explanation.definitionFit: To select is to choose, the verb in the third person.
